Let the line through \(B=(0,-1,3)\) and \(C=(2,-3,-1)\) have direction vector

\[
\vec d = C-B = (2,-3,-1)-(0,-1,3)=(2,-2,-4).
\]

A simpler direction vector is

\[
\vec d=(1,-1,-2).
\]

The foot of the perpendicular from \(A=(1,8,4)\) to the line is

\[
P = B + t\vec d
\]

where \(t\) is chosen so that \(A-P\) is perpendicular to \(\vec d\). Thus,

\[
(A-B)\cdot \vec d = t(\vec d\cdot \vec d).
\]

Now,

\[
A-B=(1,9,1).
\]

So,

\[
(A-B)\cdot \vec d = (1,9,1)\cdot(1,-1,-2)=1-9-2=-10,
\]

and

\[
\vec d\cdot \vec d=1^2+(-1)^2+(-2)^2=6.
\]

Therefore,

\[
t=\frac{-10}{6}=-\frac{5}{3}.
\]

So the foot is

\[
P=B+t\vec d=(0,-1,3)-\frac{5}{3}(1,-1,-2).
\]

\[
P=\left(-\frac{5}{3},\,-1+\frac{5}{3},\,3+\frac{10}{3}\right)
=\left(-\frac{5}{3},\,\frac{2}{3},\,\frac{19}{3}\right).
\]

The answer is \(\left(-\frac{5}{3},\frac{2}{3},\frac{19}{3}\right)\).
